name: spinner
title: Spinner
description: An indeterminate wait, rotating until the work finishes.
docs:
## When to use - An action the user just triggered: save, send, invite, publish. The spinner sits where the user is looking — inside the button, or immediately beside it. - A wait with no measurable progress: a request that returns when it returns. - A region that is loading and whose shape you cannot predict. When you *can* predict it, use `skeleton` instead: it keeps the layout stable. ## When not to use - A wait under about 300 ms. The spinner appears and disappears before it can be read, which reads as a flicker. Keep the button's label and disable it. - A known percentage. Use `progress`; a spinning wheel after "60%" is a regression. - A page that is loading its first paint. There is nothing to spin inside yet — a skeleton or a server-rendered shell is better. - A decorative "we're working on it" on a marketing page. Motion without a state change is decoration (P9). ## Installation ```bash npx shadcn@latest add @cadence/spinner ``` ## Usage ```tsx import { Spinner } from "@/components/cadence/spinner/spinner"; export function LoadingRegistry() { return (
Loading the registry…
); } ``` ## Examples ### Inside a button The button keeps its width because the spinner replaces nothing: keep the label and put the spinner in front of it, or reserve the label's space with `aria-live`. ```tsx ``` ### Sized by the caller The icon is `size-4` by default and inherits `currentColor`, so one class resizes and recolours it. ```tsx ``` ### A specific label "Loading" is the default. Say what is loading when the surrounding text does not. ```tsx ``` ### Under `data-motion="none"` The rotation stops; the icon stays and the label still says "Loading". A stopped spinner is still a state, which is why `none` does not remove it from the tree. ```tsx ``` ## API | Prop | Type | Default | Description | | ----------- | -------- | ----------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- | | `className` | `string` | – | Merged last — size and colour live here (`size-3`, `text-…`). | | `aria-label`| `string` | `"Loading"` | The accessible name; pass a specific one when it helps. | All native `svg` props are forwarded. `data-slot="spinner"` and `data-motion` are always set, and `role="status"` with the label is the announcement. ## Motion contract Recipe: `data.transition`, continuous form. The loop is CSS (`animate-spin`) rather than Motion, for the same reason as `skeleton`: a spinner is by definition next to work the user is waiting on, and it must not add a frame callback to it. Only `transform` (rotation) changes, so the loop can never trigger layout. | Phase | Properties | Token | Interruptible | | ------- | ------------------- | ----------------------------- | ------------- | | spin | `rotate 0 → 360deg` | `animate-spin` (theme timing) | yes (CSS) | | reduced | same rotation | `animate-spin` | yes (CSS) | | none | none; icon static | `animate-none` | – | Reduced keeps the rotation on purpose: M5 removes travel and scale, and a rotation in place is neither. A spinner that freezes under reduced motion would read as a frozen app. `none` stops it completely, which is what a screenshot test or a print stylesheet needs. ## Keyboard interactions None. The spinner is not focusable and takes no input; focus stays on the control that started the work, which is where the user's next action will be. ## Accessibility - `role="status"` is a polite live region: the label is announced when the spinner appears, without interrupting. Do not wrap it in another `aria-live` region. - The label must carry the meaning. The rotation is never the only signal, and under `data-motion="none"` it is not a signal at all. - Give the busy region `aria-busy="true"` and remove it when the work finishes, so the state survives even if the spinner unmounts early. - Do not replace a button's label with a spinner and nothing else. Keep the word, or add an `sr-only` copy, or the control loses its name mid-action. - Do not stack spinners. One per action; a page with five is a page with no feedback. ## Responsive behavior The spinner is an inline icon, so it follows the text it sits in. Inside a button it keeps the button's height; inside a heading, size it down (`size-3`) or it will dominate the line. On touch targets, keep the surrounding button at least 44×44 by size, not by growing the icon. ## Performance - One CSS animation per element, on `transform` only; no JS loop, no layout read. - Compositor-friendly, but the animation-system budget still applies: fewer than twenty simultaneously animating elements. For a list of pending rows, render one spinner for the list, not one per row. - No `will-change`: the browser promotes a transform animation on its own. ## Notes for AI - Use `spinner` for an action, `skeleton` for a layout. Getting this backwards is the most common loading-state mistake: a skeleton in a button, or a spinner where the content shape was known all along. - Keep the button's text; add the spinner in front of it and disable the button. - Under `data-motion="none"` the icon stays visible. Do not hide it to "respect" the preference — the state still has to be visible.
